newsitem.title: ITALY: Eurostat nod seen for Italy Eurotax-Istat official.
newsitem.headline: Eurostat nod seen for Italy Eurotax-Istat official.

text.p: Italy should get the green light from European statistics body Eurostat for its one-off Eurotax and accounting of financial guarantees for state railways, a top official at Italian statistics institute Istat said on Tuesday.

Enrico Giovannini, director of economic statistics at Istat and member of the executive body of the Eurostat monetary and financial statistics committee, confirmed Eurostat would make a decision on both issues by the end of February.
Giovannini, speaking to reporters, added: "In our opinion there's no problem."
Eurostat on Monday gave its approval for accounting methods which would result in a reduction of Italy's projected deficit to gross domestic product ratio by 0.26 percent.

But the statistics body did not rule on Italy's proposed Eurotax, a special contribution designed to reduce Italy's budget deficit further in its efforts to meet European economic and monetary union criteria, nor did it give an opinion on proposed accounting for railway guarantees.
Giovannini said: "Around February 20 there will be a series of meetings in which various subjects will probably be discussed."
The part of the Eurotax under scrutiny is some two to three trillion lire due to come from bringing forward a tax on severance payments, but Giovannini said Istat thought there would be no problem.
Accounting for financial guarantees for state railways was very complicated, he said. "But we think the treatment is consistent with the (European economic accounts system)."

Italy wants to count only the interest payments on the rail guarantees in its public sector deficit. The principle would go directly under the heading of debt without affecting the annual public sector deficit.
